messages:
dmitri: Heads-up — saw a 3s tail latency spike for a handful of dedicated-slice allocations in eu-west3 around 08:14 UTC. telemetry shows NIC burst + gpu stall correlation.
carla: ugh. any packet-drops?
dmitri: not significant drops, more like kernel tx/backlog churn. NIC softirq wait jumps then GPU stalls (kern logs show NVLINK+net driver warnings). attaching quick grep: `grep -E "softirq|tx-queue" /var/log/node-*.log | tail -n 40`
ben: can you paste the exact node ids so we can check firmware versions?
dmitri: node-rack12-03 and node-rack12-05. both on net-driver 1.2.8, fw 4.11.5. GPU driver 525.89.02.
carla: those two are in dedicated pool alpha-claim (reserved). impact visible on 3 tenants but mostly tenant:realtime-play where infer spikes and requests time out.
alice: is this noisy-neighbor or platform NIC behavior?
dmitri: looks like NIC burst -> kernel qdisc backlog -> driver stalls NVLINK queues temporarily -> cuda scheduling backs up -> allocator sees long tail for token generation. multi-tenant amplification because slab scheduling tries to coalesce.
ben: interesting. any PCIe errors?
dmitri: no ECC, but `dmesg` shows `NETDEV WATCHDOG` for ens192 around same time. stacktrace points to tx cleanup spending >500ms.
carla: propose we soft-quarantine affected tenant slices for 10m next time to avoid timeouts while we triage. avoids full eviction and cost churn.
ben: agree. soft-quarantine = signal scheduler to move new allocs to warm pool and throttle egress?
alice: +1. also think we should add NIC backlog metric to warmpool scoring. if tx-queue depth > X then prevent new allocations to that host.
dmitri: implemented a probe in local branch: `egctl probe nic-backlog --nodes node-rack12-03 --threshold 80` — returns 92% at spike.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary-deploy started for `soft-quarantine-v1` to eu-west3 (2 nodes).
carla: let's run a 1h canary with tenant sampling 5% and monitor 95/99 latencies + error-rate. keep cost delta small.
ben: cost question — if we route away from dedicated slice to warm pool we may increase per-token cost due to quantized model variant. acceptable for short quarantine, but need to track unit-cost impact.
alice: add a cost-rule to quarantine policy: if reroute increases per-token > 1.5x, only soft-quarantine for 5m and then fall back to retries.
dmitri: noted. also want to collect pcap from the NIC during next spike. command: `tcpdump -i ens192 -w /tmp/node-r12-03.pcap -c 100000` (we'll filter BPF to tenant subnets).
carla: can infra-sre run that during the canary window?
ben: I can schedule it. will also check firmware CVEs and vendor notes for tx watchdog regressions.
alice: action items: 1) run 1h canary soft-quarantine (carla + ben) 2) add nic-backlog -> warmpool gating in scheduler (alice) 3) collect pcap + dmesg + driver logs for nodes (ben) 4) cost-safety guard in policy (dmitri).
dmitri: I'll open a short runbook snippet for oncall: how to trigger soft-quarantine, quick checks, and rollback.
carla: thanks. if canary looks good we'll roll to eu-west wide and add alerting. :thumbsup:
ben: FYI I'll trim warm-pool headroom by 2 GPUs to keep cost bounded during canary.
infra-bot: incident-bot: new runbook created: `gpu-nic-burst-soft-quarantine` (link: https://confluence.company/gpu-nic-burst-soft-quarantine)
dmitri: cool. I'll post results in this thread after canary (expect data ~09:30 UTC).
alice: cheers.
carla: closing loop — remember to tag tenant owners so they can warm-retry.
ben: ping @tenant-oncall if we hit timeouts.
